headline: Recommended zoning changes for 95 Vernon St., 25 West Chester St., 128 Providence St., and 321 Green Wood St.; held inclusionary housing payment proposal.
summary: Recommended approval of zoning changes for four properties, each on a 3-0 roll call vote. The changes cover an overlay district for 95 Vernon St., rezoning of 25 West Chester St., an extension of RG-5 and the overlay district to 128 Providence St., and a zone change for part of 321 Green Wood St. Also recommended holding a driveway and pavement ordinance and a proposal to raise the inclusionary housing payment from 3% to 5%.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the September 16, 2026 committee meeting, 3-0.
Recommended approval of the Adaptive Re-use Overlay District for 95 Vernon St., 3-0.
Recommended rezoning 25 West Chester St. to Residence, Limited (RL-7), 3-0.
Recommended extending RG-5 and the Adaptive Re-use Overlay District to 128 Providence St., 3-0.
Recommended changing part of 321 Green Wood St. from ML-0.5 to BL-1.0 zoning, 3-0.
Recommended holding the zoning ordinance amendment on driveways, pavement, and permits, 3-0.
Recommended holding the proposal to raise the inclusionary housing payment from 3% to 5%, 3-0.

1. William Hughes, Worcester resident, spoke in opposition to item #3b

Chairperson Councilor Bergman recognized Councilor Mitra, who discussed the public 
participation at the Planning Board hearing for the item and plans concerning seeking 
discretionary permits for the project with Speaker #2.
Chairperson Councilor Bergman recognized the Assistant Chief Development Officer, who 
provided an overview of the item, including the favorable recommendation from the Planning

Chairperson Councilor Bergman recognized Councilor Mitra, who discussed concerns related to 
increased traffic in the area with new housing development as the streets are narrow and steep 
with the Assistant Chief Development Officer.  
Chairperson Councilor Bergman recognized Councilor Toomey, who discussed the traffic volume 
in the area when the Mercy Center was in operation, the number of units that the new housing 
development will have and concerns and plans related to remediation for stormwater management 
in the area with the Assistant Chief Development Officer and Speaker #2.

concerning making improvements to Inman Ave ., whether there are catch basins installed on the 
street, the private street status of Inman Ave ., residents’ concerns related to stormwater 
management, the residents’ rights to pass on the driveway of the property, the by right property 
usage for RS -7 zoning and new zoning legislations, whether the development will be used for a 
market rate housing project and whether the developer is amenable to plans related to installing 
speed humps on the street with Speaker #2, the Assistant Chief Development Officer and the Chief 
Development Officer.

rezone the designated area to a Residence, Limited (RL-7) zoning district.

. Miscellaneous Item 4 
October 27, 2026 Page 6 of 8Economic Development Committee
Order of Councilor Robert A. Bilotta - Request Standing Committee on Economic 
Development hold a public discussion relative to adjusting the city’s Zoning Book to 
amend Section 5 of the city’s Inclusionary Zoning Ordinance to increase the Payment in 
Lieu of constructing affordable housing from three (3) percent to five (5) percent of the 
total construction value of all building permits for the development, including trade 
permits (see attached for current ordinance).
# 10u CC June 2, 2026
a.
Chairperson Councilor Bergman read the item and recognized the following Speakers:
1. Jonathan Morales, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of item #4a 
Chairperson Councilor Bergman recognized the Chief Development Officer, who discussed how 
funding from the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) has impacted the Affordable Housing Trust 
Fund, current funding resources available for the Affordable Housing Trust Fund, the 
Inclusionary Zoning ordinance and concerns regarding fee increases and market pressures.
Chairperson Councilor Bergman recognized the Assistant Chief Development Officer, who 
discussed the need to complete additional economic feasibility studies due to the requirements 
associated with ensuring MBTA compliant zoning in some areas of the city.
Chairperson Councilor Bergman recognized Councilor Toomey, who discussed the collection 
schedule for payment in lieu fees and the feasibility of collecting the fees earlier in the process with 
the Chief Development Officer.
Chairperson Councilor Bergman recognized Councilor Mitra, who discussed the importance of 
advertising the meeting to ensure the public can weigh in on certain projects.
Chairperson Councilor Bergman then discussed the payment in lieu fee structure, the projects 
that are currently paying the payment in lieu fees, the percentage of projects being undertaken for 
units that are for rent versus for sale, the feasibility of tracking housing units that are being built 
by their for rent /for sale classification and data regarding any communities that have waived 
payment in lieu of fees in order to promote home ownership with the Chief Development Officer 
and the Assistant Chief Development Officer.
Chairperson Councilor Bergman brought forth the following Chairman’s Order: Request City 
Manager provide City Council with a report detailing the pros and cons of exempting developers 
who are building for -sale housing units from the city’s Inclusionary Zoning Ordinance’s three (3) 
percent payment in lieu of constructing affordable housing for housing developments. 
Chairperson Councilor Bergman moved for a roll call vote to recommend the item be held. 
Recommend Hold on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays
